units.en: "If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst at once into the sky, that would be like the splendor of the mighty one ... Now I am become Death, the shatterer of worlds." — J. Robert Oppenheimer, referencing the Bhagavad Gita, upon witnessing the Trinity nuclear bomb tests

In real life, the Second World War saw the first development, deployment and (currently only) active use of nuclear bombs, so they are available as a gameplay option. They are extremely powerful weapons, but are both time- and resource-consuming to manufacture. Still, whoever gains the ability to use them, will be able to obliterate their enemies' warfighting abilities and shatter their opposition from very far away. This is the Wonder Weapon that opens the path to victory, and mass destruction. Once it is researched, both warfare and the world in general will never truly be the same again.
Deploying nuclear bombs requires first researching the relevant ⟦0⟧, completion of the special projects, and specific aircraft to deliver the bombs.
The ⟦0⟧ technology serves as the prerequisite for the nuclear special projects, and gives a ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ research speed bonus.

The ⟦0⟧ special project unlocks the state level building titled "Nuclear Reactor" which can be found in the ⟦1⟧ screen. Built nuclear reactors provide the state with enriched uranium for use in nuclear weapons, but have no effect without the requisite technology to make nuclear bombs.

The ⟦0⟧ special project allows the country to produce and stockpile nuclear bombs, with one free bomb produced on project completion to conduct the initial test with. Each reactor will provide 1 bomb per 7 years (2,555 days)⟦1⟧ divided by various values. Once researched, nuclear bombs are produced by building one of three types of ⟦2⟧s; those being the Nuclear reactor, Heavy water nuclear reactor and the Civilian nuclear reactor.

The heavy-water reactor produces 1 nuclear bomb per 1278 days (3,5 years)⟦0⟧ and 1 thermonuclear bomb per 2555 days (7 years)⟦1⟧ while the other two produce 1 nuclear bomb per 852 days (2,34 years)⟦2⟧ and 1 thermonuclear bomb per 1278 days (3,5 years)⟦3⟧. The bomb production progress can be seen in the tooltip of the nuclear weapons stockpile counter on the topbar.

With the ⟦0⟧ DLC, subsequent projects enable the more powerful ⟦1⟧, the ⟦2⟧ which gives state-wide industry bonuses, ⟦3⟧ for ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧ which unlocks the Medium Range Ballistic Missile (MRBM) and the Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) for launching nuclear strikes with ⟦6⟧. Thermonuclear bombs are produced in parallel to ordinary nuclear bombs.
It is possible to speed up research by employing a ⟦0⟧ with either the Nuclear Scientist or Nuclear Enthusiast trait, and by finishing certain focuses.
How to drop a nuclear bomb

With ⟦0⟧ accompanying the release of ⟦1⟧, use of nuclear bombs has been integrated into the ⟦2⟧ interface, accessible from the bottom-right of the screen. There are two types of nuclear strikes; bomber strikes and missile strikes, both of which require a payload and delivery units. For bomber strikes, a strategic bomber wing is required, while for ⟦3⟧ strikes, an MRBM or ICBM is required. The bombers are launched from Air Bases while the missiles are launched from Rocket Sites or from a ⟦4⟧ deployed from a Naval base. All must be within range of the target to be carried out, which is dependent on the operational range of the bombers, the missiles and the submarine carrying them. And that range can become quite immense; a nuclear submarine carrying ICBMs can reach and strike practically anywhere; the submarine can travel halfway across the world from the Naval base it is stationed at, and its ICBMs can travel the same distance further from that. Once a nation has researched and developed all three delivery methods (bombers, terrestrial missiles and submarine missiles), they will have access to the full Nuclear trifecta.
If a Nuclear bomb is detonated, it will have the following effects:

Units in the province take a random percentage between 10%⟦0⟧ and 90%⟦1⟧ of their current strength and organization as damage. If a Thermonuclear bomb was used, this will apply to units in all provinces within the state, regardless of nationality. Because of this, players will want to generally avoid using Thermonuclear bombs in frontline states to avoid severe friendly fire.

The controller of the target province loses up to 20%⟦0⟧ war support. If the largest victory point in the state is smaller than 3⟦1⟧ or the undamaged infrastructure is lower than level 10, the effect is proportionately lower respectively
The first use, as well as uses on specific (capital) cities, will generate unique ⟦0⟧, however those are purely informational
